Today, we are meeting to hold a public hearing on this nomination. The Conflicts of Interest Board is the entity that serves to provide clear guidance to public employees regarding the Conflicts of Interest laws codified in Chapter 68 of the New York City Charter. The Board is tasked with achieving this goal through training, education, and the issuance and publication of advisory opinions relating to the conduct that may violate the City Conflict of Interest law. The Board also adopts rules to implement and interpret the provisions of the Conflicts of Interest laws. The Board consists of five members, three of whom are appointed by the Mayor, one appointed by the Public Advocate, and one appointed by the Comptroller, all subject to the advice and consent of the City Council. The Mayor must designate one of these members as Chair of the Board. The Charter states that all members should be chosen for their independence, integrity, civic commitment, and high ethical standards. Board members serve for staggered six-year terms and are prohibited from serving more than two consecutive six-year terms. Board members are required to meet at least once a month and are prohibited from holding public office, seeking election to any other public office, being a public employee at any jurisdiction, holding a political party office, or appearing as a lobbyist before the City. Board members are entitled to receive compensation in the amount of 250 dollars for each calendar day they perform work for the Board.
